classification.difficultyReason: Uses a negative landing displacement and a quadratic equation to find flight time, then horizontal distance.

content.prompt: A ball is thrown from a window $16\text{ m}$ above the ground. The angle of projection is $60^\circ$, initial speed is $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Using $g=10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, find:

children.label: a
children.prompt: the time taken to land (to 1 d.p.),

answer.worked:
Take the window as the origin, with upwards positive. Ground level is $y=-16$.
$$\begin{align*}
\dot{x}&=5\cos60^\circ=2.5\\
\dot{y}&=-10t+5\sin60^\circ=-10t+2.5\sqrt3\\
x&=2.5t\\
y&=-5t^2+2.5\sqrt3\,t\\
-16&=-5t^2+2.5\sqrt3\,t\\
5t^2-2.5\sqrt3\,t-16&=0\\
10t^2-5\sqrt3\,t-32&=0\\
t&=\frac{5\sqrt3+\sqrt{75+1280}}{20}\\
t&\approx2.3\text{ s}
\end{align*}$$
The negative root is rejected because $t>0$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: how far from the base of the building it lands (to 1 d.p.).

answer.worked:
Using the unrounded flight time,
$$\begin{align*}
x&=2.5\left(\frac{5\sqrt3+\sqrt{1355}}{20}\right)\\
x&\approx5.7\text{ m}.
\end{align*}$$
